theme: The Hidden Cost of Running a Corporate Event In-House

linkedin.text:
A message for every HR or Marketing leader who has ever planned a major company event while also doing their actual job:

You know the feeling.

It starts three months out — a side project. Then six weeks before the event, it has quietly consumed your calendar, your evenings and your headspace. You're cc'd on conversations between the AV company and the venue. You're fielding a question about napkin folds at 11 PM.

And the worst part: on the day itself, you're so deep in operational firefighting that you don't experience the event you built.

That's the hidden cost nobody puts in the line-item budget.

The companies that come to us have usually tried the in-house route at least once. What changes their mind isn't price. It's the moment they realize their most valuable people were spending their highest-leverage hours managing logistics instead of leading.

We've run 1,500+ events since 2010 — conferences, product launches, gala dinners, incentive trips — across 130+ destinations. The brief is always the same: your team shows up, does the important work, and goes home proud. We handle everything in between.

If your next event is coming up and you're already feeling the weight of it — DM me. No pitch, just a straight conversation about what works.
